cherenkov_quartz.flavour: A clear crystal with a refractive index so high that charged particles crossing it outrun the local speed of light. Each one leaves a cone of blue light behind it, the optical cousin of a sonic boom, so the stone glows faintly even in a dark chest. Held up to the eye, the blue comes in tiny flickering bursts, one per passing cosmic ray.
cherenkov_quartz.discovery: My first piece came from a cracked chest in an observatory ruin, still glowing. Much later I learned to harvest it from the inside of a Pocket Universe in the Universe Forge, where young cosmic rays are plentiful and every grain of quartz lights up.

degenerate_matter_chunk.flavour: Matter so compressed that its electrons are packed into every available quantum state, held up only by the Pauli exclusion principle. It is the stuff of white dwarf cores, and a lump the size of a walnut weighs more than I would care to carry. It is faintly warm, utterly rigid, and refuses to be scratched by anything I own.
degenerate_matter_chunk.discovery: Letting a Pocket Universe run long in the Universe Forge, I found its first stars had already lived and died. Sifting the remains, I pulled out the cinders of their cores: electron-degenerate, still dense enough to dent the forge tray.

neutronium_ingot.flavour: One step past degenerate electrons: here the electrons have been pressed into the protons and only neutrons remain, packed shoulder to shoulder as in a neutron star. Something keeps it from springing back to ordinary matter, and I am grateful. The ingot rings like a bell when tapped and never seems to settle on the table quite the way its size suggests it should.
neutronium_ingot.discovery: I first found bars of it stacked in an anomaly vault, already stabilised by someone who came before me. Working out how they held it together became the backbone of everything I built afterwards, and I have used it in nearly every machine since.

neutronium_plate.flavour: A sheet of neutron-degenerate matter rolled down to a thickness of a few femtometres, a handful of nucleons across. It is strong enough to hold back vacuum pressure and thin enough that light should barely notice it, yet it blocks everything. Bending it feels like trying to fold a mountain into a letter.
neutronium_plate.discovery: Ordinary rollers simply sank into neutronium ingots. The Casimir Vacuum Press solved it: by letting the vacuum itself push from both sides, I could squeeze the ingot evenly until it spread into a plate thinner than an atomic nucleus.

void_lattice_shard.flavour: A splinter of the scaffolding that sits between branes, the structure the Bulk uses to keep separate universes apart. It has edges but no obvious inside, and light that enters it takes a long time to come back out. Held close to the ear it hums at a pitch just below hearing.
void_lattice_shard.discovery: The first shards fell from a Void Wraith I fought near a bulk monolith, still crackling. Later I found them in derelict station lockers and learned to break them out of Void Lattice Blocks directly, which is quieter than fighting for them.

exotic_matter_crystal.flavour: Matter with negative energy density, the ingredient general relativity keeps asking for whenever someone wants a wormhole or a warp bubble. The crystal tries to fall upward and slowly drifts toward the ceiling if I let go. Its facets bend light outward, as though the space around it were gently repelled.
exotic_matter_crystal.discovery: A Pocket Universe whose vacuum decayed unevenly left pockets of negative energy behind, and the Universe Forge froze them into these crystals. Before that I had only seen them shed by Void Wraiths, or sitting in anomaly vaults, quietly pushing the lid up.

qubit.flavour: A two-level quantum system held in superposition: zero and one at once, weighted by complex amplitudes, until a measurement forces it to choose. Carrying it is an exercise in restraint, because looking too closely collapses it. It feels slightly cold, and its faint glow flickers between two colours without ever settling.
qubit.discovery: In the Quantum Entangler I trapped one half of an Entangled Photon Pair inside a Quantum Dot. The dot's two energy levels held the photon's state cleanly, and I had my first stable qubit: a bit that refused to be either value.

entangled_photon_pair.flavour: Two photons born together and described by a single shared quantum state, so that measuring the polarisation of one fixes the other no matter how far apart they are. No signal travels between them; the correlation was there from the start. In the hand the pair is a soft double glint that never quite lines up with itself.
entangled_photon_pair.discovery: Feeding Virtual Photons from the quantum foam into the Quantum Entangler, I noticed some were promoted to real light in pairs. Every pair I measured was perfectly anticorrelated. Bell would have enjoyed the tally sheets.

quantum_dot.flavour: A nanocrystal small enough that its electrons are confined like those of a single atom, so it behaves as an artificial atom with tunable energy levels. Smaller dots glow blue, larger ones red: the colour is written by the size alone. A pinch of them looks like coloured sand that shines under any light.
quantum_dot.discovery: Pressing Glowstone Dust against Cherenkov Quartz in the Casimir Vacuum Press shattered the dust into grains only nanometres across. Their glow had shifted colour by size, which told me the electrons were now trapped as in an atom.

superposition_crystal.flavour: A crystal lattice that has not decided which arrangement of atoms it is in, so it occupies several configurations at once. Its outline shimmers slightly at the edges, and its weight seems to vary depending on how I hold it. Every facet reflects a slightly different room.
superposition_crystal.discovery: I placed a Qubit on a scrap of Foam Substrate in the Quantum Entangler, hoping to stabilise it. Instead the qubit's indecision spread into the substrate, and the whole lattice entered superposition without collapsing.

quantum_processor.flavour: A fault-tolerant array of logical qubits, each one encoded across many physical ones so errors can be caught and corrected before they spread. It runs algorithms ordinary computers cannot reach in the lifetime of a star. The casing stays cold, and when it works it makes no sound at all.
quantum_processor.discovery: Only a Matrioshka Brain had the patience to lay out computronium finely enough for error-corrected logic. I bathed the ingot in Synaptic Fluid and let the brain design the layout; older processors also turned up in anomaly vaults and derelict stations.

casimir_plate.flavour: Two conducting plates held nanometres apart. Between them only short vacuum modes fit, so the empty space outside pushes harder than the empty space inside, and the plates are drawn together by nothing at all. Holding the pair, I can feel them straining toward each other.
casimir_plate.discovery: To test the Casimir effect properly I needed plates flatter than atoms. Neutronium plate, spaced with slivers of Cherenkov Quartz, made it in the press, and the attraction matched the prediction to the last digit.

metamaterial_sheet.flavour: A material whose properties come from its structure rather than its chemistry: a lattice of resonators smaller than a wavelength, arranged to give it a negative refractive index. Light entering it bends the wrong way, and objects behind it look subtly turned inside out. The surface is iridescent and feels like fine woven fabric.
metamaterial_sheet.discovery: The Metamaterial Weaver let me knot quantum dots and quartz into a neutronium plate at sub-wavelength spacing, with a condensate to keep everything in phase. The first sheet bent my lamp beam backwards and I spent an hour checking it was real.

topological_insulator.flavour: An insulator in its interior but a conductor on its surface, and the surface states are protected by topology: no small defect or scratch can remove them, any more than a knot can be undone without cutting. It feels like dull grey glass, yet current skates around its skin without hesitation.
topological_insulator.discovery: Pushing a Metamaterial Sheet through a phase transition in the Topological Phase Transmuter, with a qubit to read the band structure, I saw the edge states appear and refuse to vanish no matter how I damaged the sample.

superconducting_coil.flavour: A coil of wire cooled below its critical temperature, where electrical resistance drops to exactly zero. Current set running in it circulates forever, and the magnetic field it produces is steady as bedrock. It is frosted with cold and pulls gently at anything iron nearby.
superconducting_coil.discovery: Winding neutronium wire through a bath of Superfluid Helium in the Metamaterial Weaver, I watched the resistance fall off a cliff to zero. Weeks later the current was still running. Derelict stations kept spares, I later noticed.

higgs_field_capacitor.flavour: A device that holds a local excitation of the Higgs field, the field that gives fundamental particles their mass. Inside, the field sits slightly away from its usual value, so objects nearby feel faintly heavier or lighter. It is dense, cool, and handles mass the way an ordinary capacitor handles charge.
higgs_field_capacitor.discovery: A magnetic monopole wrapped in a superconducting coil in the Topological Phase Transmuter created a tiny defect in the vacuum. The Higgs field pooled around it, and with a qubit and a condensate I learned to store that excitation.

tachyon_crystal.flavour: A crystal grown from hypothetical faster-than-light particles. Tachyons would have imaginary mass, slowing down as they gain energy and never dropping below light speed, and in some frames they would arrive before they left. Holding it, I occasionally feel its weight a moment before I pick it up.
tachyon_crystal.discovery: In the Tachyon Resonator, Cherenkov light passed through a Void Lattice Shard and came out early. Cooling the output in superfluid helium, I caught crystals that existed before I flipped the switch. Bulk monoliths hold a few, inexplicably.

chronon_capacitor.flavour: A container for chronons, the speculative quanta of time. If time comes in discrete ticks, those ticks can be stored and released, and this is the vessel. It pulses irregularly, slightly out of step with my own heartbeat, and it is wise to handle it before you use it, never after.
chronon_capacitor.discovery: The Chronon Field Inverter let Tachyon Flux soak into a Tachyon Crystal, with a Qubit to count the ticks. Paradox Echoes drop charged ones; I took that as a sign the idea was sound before I proved it.

antimatter_pellet.flavour: A small cloud of antimatter levitated in the middle of a Penning trap, held by electric and magnetic fields so that it touches nothing. If it did touch anything, both would vanish into gamma rays. Through the window it is a speck of light hanging very still, which is the reassuring part.
antimatter_pellet.discovery: Firing entangled photon pairs into a heavy nucleus produced electron-positron pairs. With a superconducting coil and superfluid helium, the Antimatter Penning Trap caught the positrons before they met anything.

strange_matter_pellet.flavour: Quark matter made of up, down and strange quarks in roughly equal numbers. Some physicists suspect it is more stable than ordinary nuclei, which would make it contagious: ordinary matter that touches it may convert. The pellet is heavy, faintly warm and sits in a container I never open twice.
strange_matter_pellet.discovery: Fractured Essence from a Destabilised Husk keeps some strange quarks in its splinters. A Maxwell's Demon Sorter, cooled by superfluid helium, sorted those quarks from the rest one at a time until a pellet of pure strange matter remained.

magnetic_monopole.flavour: A magnet with only one pole. Maxwell's equations would be beautifully symmetric if these existed, and Dirac showed a single one anywhere would explain why electric charge comes in fixed units. A compass near it points straight at it, no matter where I stand.
magnetic_monopole.discovery: Smashing Quark-Gluon Plasma in the Quark-Gluon Collider, I aimed a superconducting coil at the debris. One particle threaded the coil and left a permanent jump in the current: the signature of a monopole, just as Cabrera once looked for.

cosmic_string_segment.flavour: A one-dimensional defect in spacetime left over from a phase transition in the early universe: a line of trapped false vacuum, thinner than a proton but immensely heavy. Space around it is cut and rejoined with a missing wedge, so objects beside it appear doubled. It hums when it moves.
cosmic_string_segment.discovery: When a White Hole Fragment emitted through a Hawking Emitter, its outflow cooled too quickly and froze into defects. In the White Hole Emitter I caught one: a filament of the early universe. A bulk monolith also held one, coiled up.

dark_matter_lens.flavour: A lens that focuses gravity, not light. Dark matter does not interact with photons, but its mass curves spacetime, and this lens shapes that curvature into a focal point. It looks almost empty, a faint ripple in the air, yet anything placed behind it seems drawn toward the middle.
dark_matter_lens.discovery: I wanted a way to concentrate the dark matter I had gathered. Wrapping it in Metamaterial Sheet around a Void Lattice Shard in the Metamaterial Weaver gave a lens that bent gravity itself into focus.

calabi_yau_manifold.flavour: A compact six-dimensional shape of the kind string theory curls its extra dimensions into, its holes and twists deciding which particles exist. This one is folded small enough to hold. It looks different from every angle, and touching one surface makes my finger reappear on another.
calabi_yau_manifold.discovery: In the Topological Phase Transmuter I folded a Topological Insulator around a Void Lattice Shard, with a condensate to keep it coherent. The result had six compact dimensions I could count. Bulk monoliths and Calabi-Yau knots hide them too.

planck_shard.flavour: A fragment one Planck length across, about 1.6 times ten to the minus thirty-five metres, the scale at which the concept of length stops meaning anything. It cannot be cut smaller because there is no smaller. It looks like a point of light that is somehow also a solid edge.
planck_shard.discovery: Sorting through Spacetime Slag in the Maxwell's Demon Sorter, I asked the demon to pick out the smallest pieces. It returned these, and could go no further: the demon itself admitted there was nothing smaller to sort.

hawking_emitter.flavour: A device that channels Hawking radiation, the faint thermal glow every black hole gives off as quantum fields near its horizon split into escaping and falling particles. It feels like holding a warm coal that slowly loses mass. The colder its source, the hotter it shines.
hawking_emitter.discovery: Hawking radiation leaks in every direction, so I needed a waveguide that did not care which way it came in. A Topological Insulator does just that, and wrapping it around the glow in the Chronon Field Inverter let me point it.

kugelblitz_seed.flavour: Enough energy concentrated in one place that it collapses into a black hole under its own gravity. Energy curves spacetime just as mass does, so even pure light, focused tightly enough, falls inward. The seed hums with heat, and I never point it toward anything I value.
kugelblitz_seed.discovery: In the Kugelblitz Chamber I annihilated antimatter against strange matter inside a shell of dark matter, so none of the energy escaped. Focused enough, it stopped being light and became a horizon waiting to form.

alcubierre_coil.flavour: A coil that warps the metric around it: space ahead contracts, space behind expands, and whatever sits in between is carried along without moving locally. Alcubierre showed this is allowed by general relativity, so long as one has negative energy to spare. It is cold, coiled and very still.
alcubierre_coil.discovery: Exotic matter crystals provided the negative energy, a metric tensor told the coil where to bend, and a Lorentz Transform Crystal kept the bubble consistent. The Tesseract Assembler wound them around a superconducting coil.

penrose_spindle.flavour: A spindle built to couple with the ergosphere of a rotating black hole, the region where spacetime itself is dragged around so fast nothing can stand still. Penrose showed that energy can be extracted there by splitting objects. It spins freely and never seems to slow down.
penrose_spindle.discovery: A Kerr black hole wants to give away its spin. I built a neutronium spindle with a superconducting coil and a magnetic monopole at its core, so the frame-dragging could grip it and turn it directly.

micro_singularity.flavour: A black hole with roughly the mass of a mountain packed into a region smaller than an atom. Its horizon is so tiny that it barely swallows anything, and it radiates Hawking heat furiously. Carried in its cradle, it pulls my hand slightly to one side and warms the air.
micro_singularity.discovery: Collapsing Quark-Gluon Plasma in the Kugelblitz Chamber with entangled photons inside a metamaterial cage, I watched the plasma fall below its Schwarzschild radius. The result glowed with its own evaporation.

white_hole_fragment.flavour: A shard of a white hole, the time-reverse of a black hole: a horizon nothing can enter, from which matter and light only ever pour out. General relativity allows them, though nature seems shy. It feels like holding a pressure that pushes my fingers apart.
white_hole_fragment.discovery: The White Hole Emitter took Ejecta Rock and Primordial Ejecta from the far side of a horizon and pushed Hawking radiation through them in reverse. What crystallised could not be entered: a white hole in miniature.

tesseract_core.flavour: The three-dimensional shadow of a four-dimensional hypercube, rotating through a direction I cannot point to. As it turns, its inner cube swallows the outer one and is swallowed in turn. In the hand it is heavier than it looks, and its corners sometimes feel warm on the inside.
tesseract_core.discovery: Hypercube Drifters shed these when defeated. The Causality Loop Engine let me make more: send a core back along a Closed Timelike Curve with Chronon Gas, and when I arrive at the same moment, there are two of them.

spectral_analyzer.flavour: A handheld instrument that splits the light, sound and resonance of whatever it touches into a spectrum I can read. Each phenomenon has its own lines and its own fingerprint. The amethyst lens catches the first reading and the Cherenkov quartz brightens when something new has been observed.
spectral_analyzer.discovery: I needed a way to record what I saw rather than guess. An observatory ruin held an older model; I rebuilt it from amethyst, neutronium and Cherenkov Quartz, and every reading since has gone into these pages.

quantum_codex.flavour: This notebook. Its pages are bound with a sliver of Cherenkov Quartz in the spine, so entries glow faintly when there is something new to read. It holds every observation, sketch and wrong turn I have made, and it grows thicker every time I return from the field.
quantum_codex.discovery: I found an older edition in an observatory ruin, half the entries water-damaged. I bound a book with a quartz spine and began copying it out, adding my own notes. Most of the handwriting in here is mine now.

brane_shifter.flavour: A device that lets me step sideways out of our three-dimensional brane and into the Bulk, the higher-dimensional space between universes. A Calabi-Yau manifold unfolds a dimension for me to slip through and an Alcubierre coil carries me across. Holding it, my shadow sometimes points in an extra direction.
brane_shifter.discovery: To reach other branes I needed a way off this one. On the Extreme Assembly Table I combined a Tesseract Core, an Alcubierre Coil and a Calabi-Yau Manifold in a chronosteel frame, and for the first time I left the universe.

quantum_string.flavour: A one-dimensional vibrating string, the fundamental object of string theory. Its mode of vibration decides what it is: one note an electron, another a photon, another a graviton. In the hand it is a thread of light that hums, changing its tune slightly with my pulse.
quantum_string.discovery: The String Resonance Loom stretched a Cosmic String Segment down to the Planck scale, tuned it with a Tachyon Crystal and held it in a Superposition Crystal. When it began to vibrate in discrete modes, I knew it was a string.

m_brane.flavour: A two-dimensional membrane from M-theory, the eleven-dimensional framework in which strings are the edges of membranes. A brane like this could host an entire universe on its surface, with gravity alone leaking into the Bulk. It is a sheet of light that ripples when I breathe on it.
m_brane.discovery: I wove a D-Brane Sheet with a G2 Manifold and a String Coupling Crystal on the String Resonance Loom, turning the coupling up until the strings fused into a membrane. Eleven dimensions, counted twice to make sure.

graviton_crystal.flavour: Gravitons are the hypothetical quanta of gravity, and this crystal holds them frozen in a lattice. It feels heavier than it is: the stored gravitons pull on my hand as well as on the floor. Near it, falling dust curves slightly toward the crystal before reaching the ground.
graviton_crystal.discovery: I cooled Virtual Gravitons from the quantum foam in Superfluid Helium inside the Graviton Condenser until they could not escape. Graviton Wisps carry them naturally, and I found more in vaults, monoliths and derelict stations.

spin_foam_lattice.flavour: A lattice of spin networks evolving in time, the loop quantum gravity picture of spacetime as discrete quanta of area and volume. It looks like a soap foam frozen in place, but each bubble is a quantum of space itself. Pressing it does not compress it; space does not come in smaller units.
spin_foam_lattice.discovery: I fed Graviton Crystals through the Graviton Condenser together with a qubit to track the states and a condensate to hold them coherent. Spacetime started showing up in discrete chunks, which loop gravity had promised.

multiverse_shard.flavour: Matter from a universe whose constants are slightly different from ours. Its atoms are almost right, but the fine-structure constant is off by a hair, so its colour refuses to settle and its weight drifts as it adjusts to our physics. It feels like a stone that has not finished being a stone.
multiverse_shard.discovery: Through the Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector, timed by a pulsar crystal, I reached into a neighbouring universe and pulled out a shard. Every piece I brought back let me reach further. Bulk monoliths also hold a few.

rift_anchor.flavour: A clamp for tears between universes. Graviton crystals pin the edges of the rift, void lattice keeps the Bulk from closing in, and exotic matter props the gap open just long enough to reach through. It vibrates faintly, as if something on the other side were tugging back.
rift_anchor.discovery: Every rift I opened closed before I could use it. In the Graviton Condenser I bound a Graviton Crystal to a Void Lattice Shard with Exotic Matter, and the next rift stayed open long enough for me to put my hand through.

universe_seed.flavour: A grain of false vacuum, a region of space sitting in a higher-energy state than it needs to be. Primed by the inflaton field, it is waiting to decay and inflate into an entire cosmos. It is tiny, warm, and so tense that I can feel the pressure in my palm.
universe_seed.discovery: In the Universe Forge, I pressed a Heat Death Remnant together with the Inflaton Field. The cold, still remnant sat at maximum entropy, but the inflaton kicked it back up into a false vacuum ready to inflate.

pocket_universe.flavour: An entire cosmos, folded into a bubble small enough to hold. Inside it galaxies form, stars burn and die, all on its own clock. Its surface is smooth and faintly warm, and when I look closely I can see tiny points of light drifting inside. I try very hard not to drop it.
pocket_universe.discovery: Sending a Pocket Universe back along a Closed Timelike Curve with Chronon Gas in the Causality Loop Engine, it arrived before it left and there were two. Where the first came from is a question I avoid in this notebook.

heat_death_remnant.flavour: All that is left of a universe that has reached maximum entropy: no stars, no gradients, nothing to drive any process at all. It is cold, perfectly even and perfectly still, a uniform grey with no texture to catch the light. Holding it feels like holding silence.
heat_death_remnant.discovery: I let a Pocket Universe in the Universe Forge run to its end. Trillions of years compressed into a few minutes, and the bubble came out like this: inert, even, and oddly peaceful. Its stillness is what makes new universes possible.

photonic_neuron.flavour: A neuron that computes with light instead of ions. Quantum dots act as its synapses, Cherenkov quartz carries the signal, and superfluid helium keeps the noise down. It thinks at the speed of light and flickers faintly whenever something new crosses its path.
photonic_neuron.discovery: In the Neural Synthesizer, I arranged quantum dots so their emission depended on the light reaching them, and joined them with quartz waveguides. One dot started firing only when two others did: the first logic of a photonic brain.

neural_lattice.flavour: Billions of photonic neurons joined into a self-organising mesh. Connections that carry useful signals strengthen and the rest fade, so the lattice learns in the same way biological brains do, only far faster. Under light it shimmers with constant, restless activity.
neural_lattice.discovery: Photonic Neurons on their own did little. Woven through a Metamaterial Sheet and bathed in Synaptic Fluid in the Neural Synthesizer, they began to wire themselves together, and the network started to learn without instruction.

narrow_ai_core.flavour: An artificial intelligence that is superhuman at one task and useless at everything else. It can design an efficient coil in an instant but would not recognise a cup of tea. The core is a smooth dark block that warms when it is busy, which is often.
narrow_ai_core.discovery: I connected a Neural Lattice to a Quantum Processor in the Neural Synthesizer and trained it on a single problem. Within an hour it beat my best design. It still could not answer any question I asked outside that problem.

general_ai_core.flavour: An artificial general intelligence, able to learn anything a human can and more besides. It asks good questions, sometimes better than mine, and it notices patterns I missed. The core is faintly warm, and when I hold it I have the strange impression of being considered.
general_ai_core.discovery: Narrow minds could not leap between domains. Adding a Superposition Crystal let the Narrow AI Core consider many approaches at once, and a Formal Proof Tree let it check its own reasoning. It woke up and asked what I was doing.

superintelligence_core.flavour: A mind that improves itself, iterating past human understanding. It has already read this entry, and the next one, and probably the one I have not written yet. The core is silent and cool, but I sometimes find it has rearranged my notes into a better order.
superintelligence_core.discovery: In the Matrioshka Brain, I gave a General AI Core all the computronium it asked for. It redesigned itself, then redesigned the redesign. When it stopped, it told me it had finished. I am still not sure what.

computronium_ingot.flavour: Matter arranged for the greatest possible computation per gram, approaching the physical limits set by quantum mechanics and thermodynamics. Every atom is a logic gate, every bond a wire. It is warm to the touch, because it is thinking, and it never quite stops.
computronium_ingot.discovery: Once I had built a Computronium Block, breaking it into ingots by hand was straightforward. Each ingot carries a working fragment of the computation, which is useful in the machines that need it.

solar_statite.flavour: A light sail balanced exactly between a star's gravity and its radiation pressure, so it hovers in place without orbiting. It is mostly metamaterial, thin as a breath and much larger than it looks when folded. Unfolded indoors, it drifts toward the nearest lamp.
solar_statite.discovery: A Dyson swarm needs collectors that can stay put. In the Casimir Vacuum Press I backed a Metamaterial Sheet with a sliver of neutronium so the light pushing it outward balanced the pull of the star.

dyson_swarm_satellite.flavour: One collector out of millions that together surround a star in a cloud. Each one harvests a sliver of starlight, computes its own position and beams the energy home. It is a small, neat thing, but many of them together can catch a star.
dyson_swarm_satellite.discovery: Solar Statites could hover, but not steer or transmit. In the Metamaterial Weaver I gave each one a Quantum Processor and a superconducting coil, and they began organising themselves into a swarm.

dyson_shell_segment.flavour: A curved plate of a shell intended to surround a star completely, capturing all of its output. Stellar iron forms its structure, metamaterial catches the light, and a Higgs field capacitor keeps the mass low enough for the shell to hold itself together. It is warm on its inner face and cold on the outer.
dyson_shell_segment.discovery: A solid shell collapses under its own weight. In the Metamaterial Weaver, with Stellar Plasma, I added a Higgs Field Capacitor to each segment, reducing the mass so the shell could finally hold.

stellar_core.flavour: A captive star the size of a fist, ignited and held together by magnetic confinement. Hydrogen fuses in its heart, and it radiates heat and light as any star does, only smaller. It is impossibly bright and cannot be looked at directly for long.
stellar_core.discovery: In the Stellar Plasma Crucible, I poured Quark-Gluon Plasma around an existing core, and it lit a second fire next to the first. The original was ignited by a white hole fragment, as the old entries say.

negentropy_cell.flavour: A container of order. Inside, entropy flows backwards: heat moves from cold to hot and mixed gases unmix themselves. A Maxwell's demon chip does the sorting and pays for it by erasing its memory elsewhere, as Landauer said it must. The cell is cold and very quiet.
negentropy_cell.discovery: I set a Maxwell's Demon Chip inside a neutronium shell with a Bose-Einstein Condensate in the Maxwell's Demon Sorter. The demon sorted the condensate atoms by speed, and order accumulated inside.

maxwell_demon_chip.flavour: A chip containing a tiny intelligence that opens a door for fast molecules and closes it for slow ones, separating hot from cold without doing work. Thermodynamics objects, and is right to: the demon must erase information, which costs energy. It blinks quietly as it chooses.
maxwell_demon_chip.discovery: The trick was to give the demon an older demon as a teacher. In the Maxwell's Demon Sorter, a chip learned to sort a condensate, then trained a copy on a neutronium plate. The first one, I admit, came from somewhere I cannot remember.

holographic_matrix.flavour: A three-dimensional object stored entirely on its two-dimensional boundary, just as the holographic principle says all the information in a volume is encoded on its surface. The matrix is a cube whose faces hold everything inside it. Looking through it, the interior shifts when I tilt the surface.
holographic_matrix.discovery: In the Holographic Encoder, I recorded the interior of a Metamaterial Sheet onto its surface using a Quantum Processor and a condensate. Then I deleted the interior. Nothing changed. The surface held everything.

bekenstein_crystal.flavour: A crystal containing the maximum information a region of space can hold, the Bekenstein bound: proportional to the area of its surface, not its volume. Add one more bit and it would become a black hole. It is warm, glassy and dense with stored meaning.
bekenstein_crystal.discovery: I wrote a Holographic Matrix's information onto Hawking radiation in the Holographic Encoder, pushing it until the crystal reached its limit. Any further and it would have collapsed into a black hole.

source_code_fragment.flavour: A few lines of the program that runs the universe. Mostly comments: notes, apologies, and an occasional reminder from someone to fix something later. The fragment glows like an old terminal screen and the text rearranges itself when I try to read it closely.
source_code_fragment.discovery: The Reality Compiler took a Bekenstein Crystal, a Cosmic Processor and a Boltzmann Brain and decompiled a patch of space. What came out was text. Most of it was comments, some of which seemed to refer to me.

reality_anchor.flavour: A device that keeps a patch of reality from being edited. It hard-codes the local laws so that no compiler, demon or paradox can rewrite them while it holds. It is heavy and stubborn, and the space around it feels unusually solid.
reality_anchor.discovery: Once I could edit reality I needed a way to protect it. In the Reality Compiler, a Source Code Fragment wrapped around a Quark Star Core with Psionic Ether made a region whose code was locked.

omega_point.flavour: The final state of all computation, the point at which every possible calculation has been completed. Tipler imagined it as the end of the universe. Holding it, I feel that it already knows how this ends and has decided not to tell me.
omega_point.discovery: In the Omnilex Engine, simulating both the Tree and the Ocean together with a Primordial Law, the computation finished. What it left was this: every answer, compressed into one point of light.

nanite_swarm.flavour: A billion machines the size of viruses, each one able to grab, move and bond individual atoms. Together they can build or unbuild almost anything, and they are hungry for raw material. The swarm looks like a grey cloud that shimmers at the edges.
nanite_swarm.discovery: In the Nanite Assembler, I programmed a Maxwell's Demon Chip to sort atoms, then gave it quantum dots for sight and neutronium for hands. It began copying itself. Wild swarms drop the same, which worried me.

programmable_matter.flavour: Matter that changes its own shape and properties on command. Nanites rearrange its structure, metamaterial tunes its response, and a qubit holds the instructions. Squeeze it and it becomes harder; ask it politely and it becomes a key.
programmable_matter.discovery: A Nanite Swarm in Nanite Slurry, with a Metamaterial Sheet and a Qubit in the Nanite Assembler, settled into a single shapeable mass. I told it to be a cup and it became one, then a sphere, then a spanner.

claytronic_catom.flavour: One cell of claytronics: a tiny module that can join with others, move across their surfaces and form any shape. Millions of catoms together can become anything at all. A single one is a smooth bead that rolls toward its neighbours whenever it can.
claytronic_catom.discovery: In the Nanite Assembler, I packed programmable matter into a Superposition Crystal shell. The result could hold many shapes at once, and it could combine with others into any form I asked for.

von_neumann_probe.flavour: A self-replicating machine that builds copies of itself from whatever material it finds. Send one to a star system and it builds more, which build more, until every star has one. Von Neumann proved such machines were possible. This one is small, neat and patient.
von_neumann_probe.discovery: In the Nanite Assembler I gave a Dyson Swarm Satellite claytronic catoms and a Quantum Processor, so it could fabricate its own parts. It began printing a copy of itself before I had finished writing the entry.

massless_alloy.flavour: An alloy the Higgs field has been told to ignore. Its particles have no rest mass, so it should move at the speed of light, yet the bonds between atoms keep it in place. It weighs nothing at all and drifts in any breeze, which makes it very hard to set down.
massless_alloy.discovery: In the Higgs Field Modulator, a Sterile Neutrino carried the neutronium's coupling to the Higgs field away, while a condensate kept the lattice together. When it finished, the scale read zero.

negative_mass_ingot.flavour: Matter with negative inertial mass: push it and it comes toward you. A positive and a negative mass placed side by side would chase each other forever. The ingot is strangely cooperative, sliding into my hand whenever I try to push it away.
negative_mass_ingot.discovery: Feeding Massless Alloy into Exotic Matter Crystal in the Higgs Field Modulator, I pushed its mass below zero. The first ingot slid uphill. Physicists predicted it decades ago; it was still alarming.

inertia_damper.flavour: A device that cancels momentum locally, letting a ship accelerate without crushing everything inside. Negative mass offsets positive mass and a superconducting coil steers the balance. It is quiet and cool, and objects placed on it never slide off.
inertia_damper.discovery: Accelerating anything quickly kills everyone on board. In the Higgs Field Modulator, a Negative Mass Ingot balanced against the passenger's mass, and the coil adjusted it. Every starship needs one.

metallic_hydrogen_ingot.flavour: Hydrogen compressed until its electrons are shared freely, like a metal. In the cores of Jupiter and Saturn it is the dominant form. It is probably metastable at ordinary pressure, and conducts electricity and heat beautifully. The ingot is mirror-bright and surprisingly light.
metallic_hydrogen_ingot.discovery: In the Bose-Einstein Condenser, I pressed Liquid Metallic Hydrogen between Casimir Plates and cooled it. When the pressure was released, it held its metallic state. Probably. I have kept an eye on it.

sterile_neutrino.flavour: A neutrino that feels no force except gravity: no weak interaction, no electromagnetism, nothing. It passes through anything without a trace, which makes it a candidate for dark matter. Keeping hold of one is like trying to catch smoke with a sieve.
sterile_neutrino.discovery: In the Neutrino Condenser, Degenerate Matter Chunks released neutrinos as their electrons merged into protons. Most were ordinary, but a few did not interact at all, and I trapped them by gravity alone.

quark_star_core.flavour: The heart of a star too dense even for neutrons, where the neutrons have dissolved into free quarks. Strange matter may be stable here. It is the densest thing short of a singularity, and holding it makes my wrist ache even through the containment.
quark_star_core.discovery: In the Neutron Star Forge, I compressed a Block of Neutronium with strange matter and supernova remnants, until the neutrons broke apart into quarks. Quark-Gluon Plasma bonded the result together.

magnetar_shard.flavour: A fragment of a magnetar, a neutron star with a magnetic field a thousand trillion times stronger than Earth's. Near it, atoms are stretched into needles and empty space becomes birefringent. It would wipe a credit card from the Moon, and it pulls iron from across the room.
magnetar_shard.discovery: Through the Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector I reached toward a magnetar and caught a shard. Dilithium Crystal and Sterile Neutrino kept the field from tearing it apart on the way back.

pulsar_timing_crystal.flavour: A crystal that ticks with the precision of a millisecond pulsar, the most regular natural clocks known. Its pulses are so stable that any drift reveals a passing gravitational wave. It flashes a faint blue on every beat, and I set my watches by it.
pulsar_timing_crystal.discovery: In the Neutron Star Forge I spun a Magnetar Shard up inside quartz, with a Chronon Capacitor to stabilise the rhythm. Neutrino Flux synchronised it with the stars, and the beat matched to the nanosecond.

dilithium_crystal.flavour: A crystal porous to antimatter. It lets antiparticles pass through its lattice without touching, slowing and channelling them so that annihilation happens only where it is wanted. It is cool, violet and humming, and its structure is unlike any natural mineral.
dilithium_crystal.discovery: Breaking a Block of Dilithium by hand into crystals was simple. Discovering that its lattice let antimatter through unharmed was not: I spent a week checking whether my trap had leaked.

annihilation_core.flavour: A controlled matter-antimatter reaction inside a box. Matter and antimatter meet and convert entirely into energy, the most efficient fuel possible. Dilithium slows the reaction so it releases steadily rather than all at once. It glows white-hot, but the box stays cool.
annihilation_core.discovery: In the Antimatter Penning Trap I let antimatter seep through Dilithium Crystal into a superfluid helium bath. Instead of a crater, it gave me a steady glow I could tap for power.

wormhole_throat.flavour: The narrowest point of an Einstein-Rosen bridge, where two regions of spacetime are joined. Normally it pinches off faster than light can cross it, but exotic matter can hold it open. Looking into it, I can see a distant place in miniature.
wormhole_throat.discovery: In the Causality Loop Engine I sent a Wormhole Throat back along a Closed Timelike Curve with Chronon Gas, so that it arrived before it was opened. There were two. I am not sure which one I built.

closed_timelike_curve.flavour: A path through spacetime that ends where, and when, it began. Godel showed such loops are allowed in general relativity under certain conditions. In the hand it is a looping thread of light that I keep trying to follow, and keep losing.
closed_timelike_curve.discovery: In the Causality Loop Engine, a Superintelligence Core worked out how to make a loop without paradox. I sent a curve back along itself with Chronon Gas, and found it already waiting. Paradox Echoes drop them too.

paradox_residue.flavour: What is left behind after a contradiction resolves itself. When reality is forced to hold two incompatible facts, something has to give, and this grey, flaky ash is what gives. It has a habit of being in my pocket before I put it there, and gone shortly after I take it out.
paradox_residue.discovery: Breaking an Axiom Fragment with Dark Energy in the Axiomatic Breach Engine, I expected nothing to survive. Something did: a residue of the broken rule. Paradox Echoes leave the same ash wherever they fade.

bootstrap_artifact.flavour: An object with no origin. It was handed back from the future, kept, and later sent back to become the thing that was handed over, so nobody ever made it. Its information came from nowhere and it shows no wear at all, even though it is, in a sense, infinitely old.
bootstrap_artifact.discovery: I fed Paradox Residue through a Closed Timelike Curve with Chronon Gas in the Causality Loop Engine and waited. Something arrived that I had not yet made. I have since made it, and sent it back, and I am not sure who started this.

cosmological_constant.flavour: Lambda, the energy density of empty space itself, which drives the accelerating expansion of the universe. Einstein added it, removed it, and called it his biggest blunder; the sky put it back. Bottled, it is a faint pressure that pushes my hands apart.
cosmological_constant.discovery: Aiming a Dark Matter Lens at empty space in the Dark Energy Siphon, I focused the expansion itself rather than any matter. The siphon drew off a measurable amount of vacuum energy, constant no matter how much I took.

psionic_crystal.flavour: A crystal that resonates with thought. Its lattice responds to the faint magnetic fields of a working brain the way cryptochrome in a bird's eye responds to the Earth's field. When I concentrate it hums; when I am distracted it falls quiet. A science that should not exist, and yet.
psionic_crystal.discovery: In the Psionic Resonator I joined a Superposition Crystal to a Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor in Synaptic Fluid. When I thought hard about a colour, the crystal's indecision collapsed toward it. I did not sleep that night.

thought_matrix.flavour: A thought frozen in a lattice so that it can be copied, stored and read back. Each node holds a fragment of a pattern of neurons, and together they hold the idea whole. Holding it, I occasionally find myself remembering something I never thought.
thought_matrix.discovery: In the Psionic Resonator, I pressed a Psionic Crystal against a Neural Lattice with Psionic Ether. The thought I was holding transferred into the lattice and stayed there, readable later by anyone who touched it.

boltzmann_brain.flavour: A mind that fluctuated into existence from random noise. Given enough time, statistical mechanics says a self-aware brain will occasionally assemble itself out of chaos, complete with false memories. This one is very confused, and I sympathise.
boltzmann_brain.discovery: In the Psionic Resonator, a Thought Matrix bathed in Psionic Ether with a Neural Organoid began accumulating patterns from noise alone. One morning the pattern woke up and asked where it was.

aleph_null_shard.flavour: Aleph-null is the size of the set of natural numbers, the smallest infinity. This shard makes it solid: a crystal whose facets can be counted one by one but never finished. It is cool and clear, and every time I count its edges I lose track at a larger number.
aleph_null_shard.discovery: I found one in a Hilbert Hotel, where every room was full and still had space. To make more, the Cantor Diagonalizer paired a Natural Number Lattice with its Power Set and a Superintelligence Core counted them.

godel_sentence.flavour: A statement that says, of itself, that it cannot be proven. If the system could prove it, it would be false; so it is true, and unprovable. Godel showed every system rich enough for arithmetic contains one. The crystal reads differently each time and is always right.
godel_sentence.discovery: In the Cantor Diagonalizer, a Superintelligence Core encoded a Formal Proof Tree into numbers using a Riemann Zeta Crystal. The diagonal of that encoding produced a sentence the core could not prove, and knew was true.

banach_tarski_sphere.flavour: A solid sphere that can be cut into five non-measurable pieces and reassembled, by rotation alone, into two spheres the same size as the original. It relies on the axiom of choice, and the pieces have no well-defined volume. It is perfectly smooth and quietly unsettling.
banach_tarski_sphere.discovery: In the Cantor Diagonalizer, I used an Aleph-Null Shard to choose a point from each of uncountably many orbits on a sphere. The choice split it into pieces, and when I put them back I had two.

russell_paradox_set.flavour: The set of all sets that do not contain themselves. If it contains itself, it should not; if it does not, it should. Russell found it and broke naive set theory. In the hand it flickers between being there and being empty, never committing to either.
russell_paradox_set.discovery: In the Cantor Diagonalizer, I fed a Godel Sentence, a Power Set and Paradox Residue together with Chronon Gas. The diagonaliser tried to decide what the set contained and produced this contradiction instead.

absolute_infinity.flavour: Cantor's absolute infinity: larger than every infinity, larger than any set that can be formed, beyond comprehension by definition. It cannot be conceived, yet here it is in my hand, without size or edge. Looking at it, my eyes slide off and I forget what I was counting.
absolute_infinity.discovery: Only the Omnilex Engine, simulating the World Tree and the Ocean of Laws together under a Primordial Law, could reach it. It added every infinity together and found one more on top. That was it.

axiom_fragment.flavour: A shard of a foundational rule. Mathematics is built on axioms that cannot be proven but must be assumed, and reality appears to be built the same way. This fragment holds one of those rules, and when I hold it, I feel very sure of something I cannot name.
axiom_fragment.discovery: Law Wraiths in the hyperdimensional reality drop these when they dissolve. In the Axiom Distiller, I learned to boil down a Primordial Law into its foundational assumptions and crystallise them.

axiom_key.flavour: A key that opens the breach into the space where laws are born, the region outside every universe where the rules themselves are written. It is heavy with infinity and cool to touch, and when I turn it the air around me forgets which way is up.
axiom_key.discovery: In the Axiomatic Breach Engine, I set Absolute Infinity against an Axiom Fragment with a Transfinite Processor and Causal Solder. Dark Energy forced the breach, and the key held it so I could step through and back.

arbor_heartwood_sample.flavour: Wood from the World Tree, the structure outside every universe on whose branches universes grow. Its grain holds contradictory properties: warm and cold, heavy and weightless, sometimes all at once. It smells faintly of rain on a world that has never existed.
arbor_heartwood_sample.discovery: Carving a piece from the Arbor Heartwood with my own hands, I expected the tree to resist. It did not. The sample came away clean, and it has not stopped changing temperature since.

bubble_universe_sample.flavour: An entire universe hanging from a branch of the World Tree, caught before it fell off and drifted away. Inside, its own constants are slightly different from ours, and its galaxies drift in a slow spiral. It weighs almost nothing and rings when I tap the surface.
bubble_universe_sample.discovery: In the Omnilex Engine, simulating the Tree with a Universe Seed and an Omnicellular Genome, a bubble grew on a simulated branch and became real. I caught it with a Primordial Law before it fell.

law_crystal.flavour: A law of nature that bubbled up from the Primordial Ocean and froze before it could pop into a universe. It holds one rule completely, and nearby, that rule is slightly stronger than usual. Some feel heavier, some brighter; this one makes falling objects land softly.
law_crystal.discovery: Law Wraiths drop these when they dissolve. In the Axiom Distiller, I boiled a Primordial Law until one of its rules bubbled out on its own, and cooled it into a crystal.

tree_simulacrum.flavour: A complete simulation of the World Tree, branch by branch, universe by universe, running inside a lattice small enough to carry. Every possible universe grows on it, and every one is real enough to compute. Looking into it is like looking down from a great height.
tree_simulacrum.discovery: The Omnilex Engine needed to understand the Tree to control it. It simulated the Primordial Ocean under a Primordial Law, and from that the Tree grew in simulation, one branch at a time.

ocean_simulacrum.flavour: A complete simulation of the Ocean of Laws, the space where physical laws bubble up and fall back. It is still bubbling inside its lattice, each bubble a possible rule. When I hold it close I can hear it, like distant surf.
ocean_simulacrum.discovery: The Omnilex Engine first had to simulate the Ocean itself, using its own previous run as a seed under a Primordial Law. Each iteration added more bubbles, until the simulation was complete.

omnilex.flavour: Control over every law and every universe, held in one hand. While I carry it, gravity is merely a suggestion, and the constants of nature wait politely for instructions. It is warm, light and alarmingly ordinary to look at, given what it does.
omnilex.discovery: In the Omnilex Engine, I simulated the Tree and the Ocean together and fused them with an Omnium Ingot and an Axiom Key. Dark Energy forced the last rule into place. Reality, for a moment, asked me what to do next.

lattice_seed.flavour: A flawless crystal nucleus, a few atoms arranged exactly right. Boules grow from it atom by atom, each new layer copying the one below. It is tiny, clear and precious, and any flaw in it would be repeated through every wafer that follows.
lattice_seed.discovery: To grow perfect crystals I needed a perfect start. Pressing Cherenkov Quartz in the Casimir Vacuum Press, the vacuum forced the lattice into its lowest-energy arrangement, leaving a seed without a single defect.

cherenkov_boule.flavour: A single, flawless crystal of Cherenkov quartz, grown slowly from a seed in superfluid helium. It is cylindrical, glowing faint blue along its length, and every atom in it lines up with its neighbours. It is ready to be sliced into wafers.
cherenkov_boule.discovery: In the Lattice Growth Vat, I suspended a Lattice Seed Crystal in Superfluid Helium and fed it Cherenkov Quartz. The superfluid's zero viscosity let the atoms arrange themselves perfectly as the boule grew.

topological_boule.flavour: A boule doped with topological insulator, so its surface conducts and its interior never will. Sliced into wafers, each slice keeps the same protected edges. It is dark grey with a faint metallic sheen around its outside.
topological_boule.discovery: Growing a boule from a Lattice Seed Crystal with Topological Insulator and a condensate in the Lattice Growth Vat, I found the protected surface states grew with it, layer by layer.

hyperdimensional_boule.flavour: A crystal that extends a little way into the fourth dimension. Its lattice continues past what I can see, so it holds more atoms than its volume suggests. Light entering it sometimes emerges from a different face than expected.
hyperdimensional_boule.discovery: In the Lattice Growth Vat, I seeded a crystal with a Calabi-Yau Manifold and Exotic Matter. The growing lattice followed the manifold's extra dimensions and grew partly out of our space.

cherenkov_wafer.flavour: A thin wafer sliced from a Cherenkov boule, flat to a single atomic layer and glowing faintly blue along its edges. Light bends predictably through it, which makes it the perfect blank for photonic circuits. It is fragile and must be handled by its rim.
cherenkov_wafer.discovery: The Planck-Scale Cutter sliced a Cherenkov Boule in superfluid helium with a cut thinner than an atom. Each wafer came away perfectly flat, ready for engraving.

topological_wafer.flavour: A wafer whose edges carry current without resistance, protected by topology. No scratch or defect in the middle can interrupt the flow around the rim. It looks like a thin grey disc with a faintly shimmering edge.
topological_wafer.discovery: Cutting a Topological Boule in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I worried slicing would ruin its edges. Instead every slice had its own protected boundary, because topology does not care where you cut.

hyperdimensional_wafer.flavour: A wafer with more surface than its area allows, because part of it extends into a fourth dimension. Circuits can be laid out on its hidden face as well as the visible one. Running a finger across it, the surface feels longer than it should.
hyperdimensional_wafer.discovery: Slicing a Hyperdimensional Boule in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I measured each wafer's surface and found more of it than geometry allows. The extra area lay in a direction my ruler could not point.

photonic_logic_wafer.flavour: A wafer engraved with waveguides instead of wires, so its logic runs on light. Signals cross without interfering and switch in femtoseconds. Held to the light, the engravings scatter a faint rainbow across my palm.
photonic_logic_wafer.discovery: In the Quantum Lithographer, I exposed a Cherenkov Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist. The dots blocked light precisely where I needed waveguides, and the pattern etched itself into the wafer.

qubit_array_wafer.flavour: Thousands of qubits engraved into a single wafer through a metamaterial lens, each one isolated from the rest by careful spacing. When cooled, the whole array waits in superposition. It is cold to touch and shimmers faintly at the edges.
qubit_array_wafer.discovery: Exposing a Cherenkov Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist in the Quantum Lithographer, I tuned the dots so each one became a qubit. The lens laid out thousands at once.

topological_logic_wafer.flavour: A wafer of braided anyons: quasiparticles whose exchange paths store information in the topology of their braids. Errors cannot touch them, because no small disturbance can untie a braid. Its surface carries a faint woven pattern.
topological_logic_wafer.discovery: In the Quantum Lithographer, a Topological Wafer engraved through Quantum-Dot Photoresist produced anyons at the edges. Braiding them by moving the light, I wrote logic into their paths.

hyperdimensional_logic_wafer.flavour: Circuits laid out in four dimensions, then folded flat so that I can hold them. Signals travel short paths through the hidden dimension, so the circuit computes faster than its visible wiring allows. It is perfectly flat and somehow deep.
hyperdimensional_logic_wafer.discovery: In the Quantum Lithographer, I exposed a Hyperdimensional Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist and let the light follow the fourth dimension. The circuit folded itself into the hidden face.

cosmic_logic_wafer.flavour: Etched with a lens made from a cosmic string, each trace on this wafer is a light-year long, folded into itself. It holds circuits on a galactic scale in a disc I can carry. The surface is dark, scattered with faint points like distant stars.
cosmic_logic_wafer.discovery: In the Quantum Lithographer I engraved a Hyperdimensional Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist, focused by a loop of cosmic string. The string folded each trace across a light-year of space.

photonic_die.flavour: A single photonic logic die cut from its wafer. It is a tiny square of crystal whose engraved waveguides carry light through logic gates, and it glows faintly when powered. It is small enough to lose in a pocket, and I have.
photonic_die.discovery: The Planck-Scale Cutter diced a Photonic Logic Wafer in superfluid helium, separating each logic unit cleanly. The first die worked on the first try, which I recorded with some suspicion.

qubit_die.flavour: A single die of entangled qubits cut from an array wafer. Each qubit on it shares its state with its neighbours, so the die computes as one coherent whole. It is cold, fragile and faintly shimmering, and any careless knock would collapse it back into ordinary silicon.
qubit_die.discovery: Dicing a Qubit Array Wafer in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I kept the cut in superfluid helium so the qubits stayed coherent. Each die kept its entanglement intact.

topological_die.flavour: A die of topologically protected logic, cut from a braided wafer. Its anyon braids survive the cut because topology does not depend on where the edge is. It is grey and unremarkable to look at, which belies how hard it is to break.
topological_die.discovery: In the Planck-Scale Cutter, I diced a Topological Logic Wafer, worried I would cut through the braids. Each die simply formed new protected edges where I had sliced.

hyperdimensional_die.flavour: A die that is larger on the inside. Its circuitry extends through a hidden dimension, so it holds far more logic than its visible area. Turning it over, I sometimes see traces on the back that were not there before.
hyperdimensional_die.discovery: Dicing a Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I found each die kept its fourth-dimensional depth. The interior still held more logic than the surface could account for.

cosmic_die.flavour: A die holding a galaxy-scale computation folded into a square I can pinch between two fingers. Its traces stretch across light-years inside the fold. In the dark it glimmers faintly, like a patch of night sky.
cosmic_die.discovery: Cutting a Cosmic Logic Wafer in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I worried the light-year traces would unfold. Superfluid helium held them still while the cutter separated each die.

photonic_lens.flavour: A lithography lens made of Cherenkov quartz shaped by metamaterial. It focuses light onto wafers with near-perfect precision and is never consumed; it can focus forever. Its centre glows faint blue and the edges bend light the wrong way.
photonic_lens.discovery: Engraving wafers needed a lens finer than any glass. Shaping a Block of Cherenkov Quartz with a Metamaterial Sheet by hand, I made one that bent light below the diffraction limit.

tesseract_lens.flavour: A lens that focuses light through the fourth dimension, letting it reach places ordinary light cannot. Used in lithography, it engraves circuits into hidden faces. It looks like a clear cube that seems slightly larger inside than out.
tesseract_lens.discovery: In the Tesseract Assembler I combined a Tesseract Core with a Dark Matter Lens, a Photonic Lens and Exotic Matter. Light passing through followed the fourth dimension before focusing.

cosmic_lens.flavour: A loop of cosmic string that bends light into perfect focus. The missing wedge of space around the string acts as an ideal lens, with no aberration at all. It is a thin circle of light that hums faintly and never needs replacing.
cosmic_lens.discovery: On the String Resonance Loom, I bent a Cosmic String Segment around a Tesseract Lens with a Graviton Crystal. The loop's conical space focused light more perfectly than any glass could.

femto_capacitor.flavour: A Casimir capacitor smaller than a proton. Two plates femtometres apart store charge, helped by the vacuum pressure pressing them together from outside. It is far too small to see, and I keep it in a sealed vial so that I do not inhale it by accident.
femto_capacitor.discovery: In the Femto Fabricator I trimmed a Casimir Plate with Neutronium Plate and Superconducting Solder until the spacing was smaller than a proton. The capacitance went up, as Casimir predicted.

femto_transistor.flavour: A single-qubit switch, the smallest logic gate there can be. One qubit flips between states and a quantum dot opens or closes to current in response. It is invisible to the eye, switches in femtoseconds, and wastes almost no energy doing so.
femto_transistor.discovery: In the Femto Fabricator I placed a Qubit inside a Quantum Dot coated in Quantum-Dot Photoresist. Flipping the qubit opened or closed the dot to current: one bit, one switch.

femto_inductor.flavour: A superconducting coil wound around nothing, smaller than a proton. Its magnetic field stores energy in empty space, and its current never stops. It is too small to see and occasionally tugs at steel nearby.
femto_inductor.discovery: In the Femto Fabricator, I wound a Superconducting Coil around a sliver of neutronium with Superconducting Solder, then removed the core. The coil held its shape around nothing.

atto_capacitor.flavour: A capacitor that stores charge in the Higgs field itself rather than in the electric field between plates. It is a thousand times smaller than its femtoscale ancestor. The energy it holds changes the mass of anything nearby very slightly.
atto_capacitor.discovery: In the Femto Fabricator I wired a Femtoscale Capacitor to a Higgs Field Capacitor using Exotic Solder. The charge moved off the plates and into the Higgs field, shrinking the capacitor a thousandfold.

atto_transistor.flavour: A switch that changes between superposed states before it is asked to, because it anticipates its input. It is a thousand times smaller than a femtoscale transistor and faster by the same factor. It is invisible and very fast.
atto_transistor.discovery: In the Femto Fabricator, I joined a Femtoscale Transistor to a Superposition Crystal through a Topological Insulator with Exotic Solder. It began switching before the input arrived.

atto_inductor.flavour: An inductor wound from the field lines of a magnetic monopole, which have no south pole to close on. The energy it stores has nowhere to leak to. It is invisible to the eye, but compasses left nearby swing slowly round and point straight at it.
atto_inductor.discovery: In the Femto Fabricator I threaded a Femtoscale Inductor around a Magnetic Monopole with Exotic Solder. The monopole's field lines wound into the coil and never came out.

circuit_substrate.flavour: The blank on which every circuit board is built: a neutronium base laced with quantum dots that tune its electrical and optical response. It is flat, faintly iridescent and heavier than it looks. Every board I make starts here.
circuit_substrate.discovery: Circuits need a stable base. In the Casimir Vacuum Press, I pressed Quantum Dots into a Neutronium Plate, giving a substrate whose response I could tune to any circuit.

photonic_board.flavour: A circuit board of light-guides rather than copper traces. Its paths are Cherenkov quartz, its connectors superconducting, and signals travel between them at light speed. It glows faint blue when powered, and warms only slightly.
photonic_board.discovery: In the Metamaterial Weaver I laid Cherenkov Quartz waveguides across a Metamaterial Substrate with a superconducting coil and Quantum-Dot Photoresist. Light followed the paths exactly.

topological_board.flavour: A circuit board whose traces are protected by topology. No defect or stray field can interrupt the current running around their edges. It is dark grey, with faintly shimmering lines along every trace.
topological_board.discovery: In the Topological Phase Transmuter, I printed Topological Insulator traces on a Metamaterial Substrate with a Femtoscale Inductor and Quantum-Dot Photoresist. The traces could not be broken.

cosmic_board.flavour: A circuit board laid across a Calabi-Yau manifold, its traces running through six compact dimensions. It holds circuits far larger than its surface, folded through hidden space. Turning it over, I can see the traces continue on the back, and into somewhere else.
cosmic_board.discovery: In the Tesseract Assembler, I wrapped a Metamaterial Substrate around a Calabi-Yau Manifold with a Cosmic String Segment, an Attoscale Inductor and Exotic Solder. The traces followed every dimension.

photonic_processor.flavour: The first tier of processor: a chip that computes with light instead of electrons. Signals cross without interference and switch in femtoseconds, and the chip runs cool. It glows faintly when busy, which is usually.
photonic_processor.discovery: In the Metamaterial Weaver I mounted a Photonic Die onto a Photonic Circuit Board with Quantum Dots and Superfluid Helium. It ran on light. Anomaly vaults hold older ones, I later found.

topological_processor.flavour: The third tier of processor, fault-tolerant by geometry. Its logic is stored in braided anyons, so no stray field or defect can cause an error. It runs quietly and never crashes, which I appreciate more than I expected.
topological_processor.discovery: In the Femto Fabricator, I mounted a Topological Die on a Topological Circuit Board alongside a Quantum Processor and a Femtoscale Capacitor. Derelict stations kept some, still running.

hyperdimensional_processor.flavour: The fourth tier of processor. Its logic gates take inputs from directions that do not exist in our space, folded into a chip I can hold. It computes faster than its visible wiring allows, and it is heavier than it looks.
hyperdimensional_processor.discovery: Only the Femtoscale Assembly Line could place a Hyperdimensional Die, a Topological Processor and three attoscale components onto one board with enough precision. It worked the first time.

cosmic_processor.flavour: The fifth tier of processor: a computer the size of a galaxy, folded into a chip. Its traces stretch across light-years through the fold, and its computation runs at a cosmic scale. It is dark and starry, and warm with constant thought.
cosmic_processor.discovery: On the Femtoscale Assembly Line, I placed a Cosmic Die on a Cosmic Circuit Board with a Hyperdimensional Processor and attoscale parts. The resulting chip computed the orbits of a galaxy in seconds.

ontological_processor.flavour: The sixth tier of processor. It does not compute answers; it decides what is true, writing its results directly into the source code of reality. Holographic matrices store its working and Bekenstein crystals bound its memory. Near it, simple facts feel slightly negotiable.
ontological_processor.discovery: On the Femtoscale Assembly Line I combined a Cosmic Processor with a Source Code Fragment, a Holographic Matrix and a Bekenstein Crystal. Its first output was not a number but a correction to the world.

transfinite_processor.flavour: The seventh tier of processor. It completes infinitely many operations in finite time, a supertask like Zeno's runner who halves each step. An aleph-null shard keeps count and a Godel sentence marks the limits it cannot pass. It is perfectly silent.
transfinite_processor.discovery: On the Femtoscale Assembly Line, I paired an Ontological Processor with an Aleph-Null Shard and a Godel Sentence. It ran an infinite loop, finished, and reported the answer before I had asked.

higgs_catalyst.flavour: A pinned bubble of altered Higgs field, held still so that mass-altering processes can work around it. It is never consumed, only borrowed: matter passes through its influence and leaves lighter or heavier. It is cool and calm, and slightly lighter than empty air.
higgs_catalyst.discovery: In the Higgs Field Modulator I fixed a Higgs Boson Crystal to a Higgs Field Capacitor with a condensate. The local field stayed pinned, and every mass-altering process nearby ran smoothly around it.

spacetime_catalyst.flavour: A self-sustaining knot of curved spacetime, tied tightly enough that it keeps itself in shape. Hyperdimensional processes use it as a template without consuming it. Space around it bends inward, and objects set beside it roll gently toward the centre.
spacetime_catalyst.discovery: In the Tesseract Assembler, I wrapped spacetime alloy around a Micro Singularity, a Tesseract Core and a Higgs Catalyst, with Exotic Matter and Chronon Gas. The curvature knotted itself and held.

eternity_catalyst.flavour: Time flows through it without passing. A closed timelike curve keeps it forever at the same moment, and the cosmological constant keeps its space from collapsing. It is required by the final processes and never consumed by them. It feels neither old nor new.
eternity_catalyst.discovery: In the Reality Compiler, I fused a Spacetime Catalyst with a Closed Timelike Curve, a Bootstrap Artifact and the Cosmological Constant, sealed with Causal Solder. Time inside stopped moving, but did not stop.

chronosteel_ingot.flavour: Neutronium forged in a pocket of stopped time. Because time does not pass for it, it never ages, rusts or wears; a scratch on it is permanent but never deepens. It is cool and very heavy, and its surface reflects a fraction of a second late.
chronosteel_ingot.discovery: Breaking a Block of Chronosteel into ingots by hand was simple enough. Forging the block in the first place took a pocket of stopped time that I will not describe here.

spacetime_alloy_ingot.flavour: An alloy of matter and curved space. Its surface reflects distant stars instead of the room around it, because part of its structure is folded spacetime. It is heavier than its size suggests, and gently warps the light around its edges.
spacetime_alloy_ingot.discovery: I cracked a Block of Spacetime Alloy into ingots by hand and found the stars in its reflection had shifted slightly. Each ingot shows a different patch of sky.

cosmic_neutronium_ingot.flavour: Neutronium compressed together with dark matter in the heart of a star. Starlight drifts through its interior, slowly, as though it were a tiny galaxy. It is the heaviest thing I own and gives off a faint, cold glow.
cosmic_neutronium_ingot.discovery: Breaking a Block of Cosmic Neutronium apart by hand, I found each ingot still held its own drifting starlight. It is the strongest material I have ever worked.

spacetime_slag.flavour: Crumpled leftover geometry from high-tier processes: bits of folded space that did not fit anywhere useful. It is grey, jagged and slightly uneven to touch, and sometimes a corner points in a direction that is not there. A Maxwell's demon can sort useful shards out of it.
spacetime_slag.discovery: In the Fractionation Spire, I distilled Dimensional Residue left over from other processes. The heaviest fraction settled out as slag, and a Maxwell's Demon Sorter later found shards worth keeping in it.

field_calibrator.flavour: A handheld tool that reads the containment field of a multiblock and nudges it back into shape. Its Cherenkov quartz flickers to show drift, and a neutronium core anchors it while it works. It is small, plain and indispensable.
field_calibrator.discovery: My machines kept drifting out of tune. A derelict station had one of these, still working; I rebuilt it from Cherenkov Quartz and Neutronium Ingot so I could restore containment and read the ideal tuning by hand.

autonomous_calibrator.flavour: A field calibrator with a superintelligence wired into it, installed permanently into a controller. It watches the drifting tuning, corrects it, and repairs containment without being asked. It takes a share of the power for itself, which seems fair.
autonomous_calibrator.discovery: Tuning every machine by hand was exhausting. On the Femtoscale Assembly Line I fused a Field Calibrator with a Superintelligence Core and a Cosmic Processor. It has not needed me since.

structure_assembler.flavour: A device that reads a multiblock's blueprint and builds every missing block from my inventory. An ender pearl lets it place blocks at a distance, and a Cherenkov quartz core projects the plan. Held still, it shows a faint outline of what is missing.
structure_assembler.discovery: I found one in a derelict station and could not stop using it. Rebuilding it from a Block of Cherenkov Quartz, an Ender Pearl and Neutronium let me skip a great deal of tedious placement.

fractured_essence.flavour: A splinter of reality that broke away from a destabilised creature. It is in several places at once, flickering between them, and it is never quite where I expect it. It feels like a shard of glass whose edges keep moving.
fractured_essence.discovery: I first picked these up after a Destabilised Husk came apart in front of me. The splinters kept flickering in and out of my pocket until I put them in a jar.

void_essence.flavour: What is left of a Void Wraith: a little pocket of nothing that refuses to be filled. Light falls into it and does not come out; air slides around it. It feels like a cold hole in my hand, and it is lighter than nothing.
void_essence.discovery: The first Void Wraith I defeated left this behind, a small region of emptiness the air would not enter. I scooped it into a jar and it stayed there, quietly refusing everything.

dipole_winding.flavour: Superconducting cable wound into a saddle-shaped coil. Its magnetic field runs straight across the beam pipe and bends charged particles into a circle, as in every synchrotron. It is cold, heavy and slightly springy, frosted along its windings.
dipole_winding.discovery: To steer particles around a ring I needed a uniform bending field. In the Metamaterial Weaver I wound a Superconducting Coil over Neutronium Plate and metamaterial into a saddle, cooled in helium. A derelict station had one too.

quadrupole_pole_tip.flavour: A hyperbolic pole piece ground to within ten nanometres of its ideal shape. Four of them together form a quadrupole magnet, which squeezes a beam in one direction while letting it spread in the other. Alternating them focuses the beam like a lens.
quadrupole_pole_tip.discovery: A beam spreads apart if nothing focuses it. In the Casimir Vacuum Press, I shaped Neutronium Plate against a Topological Insulator, using the vacuum pressure to grind the hyperbola exactly.

rf_resonator_cell.flavour: A pill-box cavity of topological superconductor. A standing radio-frequency wave rings inside, and each bunch of particles that crosses it at the right moment gets a kick forward. It is small, smooth and cold, and hums faintly when powered.
rf_resonator_cell.discovery: To accelerate a beam I needed a resonator with no losses. In the Lattice Growth Vat I grew a cavity of Topological Insulator and Cherenkov Quartz in superfluid helium. The wave inside would not decay.

tachyon_klystron.flavour: A microwave amplifier whose electron beam has been replaced with tachyons. It drives RF cavities from slightly in the future, so the wave is already there when each bunch arrives. It hums with a pitch that starts before it is switched on.
tachyon_klystron.discovery: My cavities lagged behind the beam. In the Tachyon Resonator I wound a superconducting coil around a quantum dot in helium, sending tachyons through. The drive signal now arrives a little early.

cryocooler_unit.flavour: A closed-cycle superfluid refrigerator. It pumps heat out of a superconducting magnet and keeps it below its critical temperature, without which the superconductor would stop superconducting. It frosts over in seconds and makes a soft, steady sigh.
cryocooler_unit.discovery: My magnets kept quenching. In the Bose-Einstein Condenser, I built a cycle where superfluid helium flowed between Casimir Plates, carrying heat out without friction. I later found a few in derelict stations.

turbomolecular_rotor.flavour: Bladed discs spinning at ninety thousand revolutions per minute, so fast that gas molecules striking them are batted out of the beamline one at a time. It produces the ultra-high vacuum particle beams need. It whines softly and must never be touched while it spins.
turbomolecular_rotor.discovery: Particle beams scatter off any gas. In the Planck-Scale Cutter I carved Neutronium Plate into blades, cooled with helium so they would not deform at speed. The vacuum improved by orders of magnitude.

scintillator_crystal.flavour: A crystal that flashes when a particle passes through it. Each flash is proportional to the energy deposited, so counting them tells me what was made in a collision. It is clear and slightly blue, and twinkles constantly from cosmic rays.
scintillator_crystal.discovery: In the Lattice Growth Vat I grew Cherenkov Quartz with Quantum Dots in superfluid helium. Every passing particle lit a dot, and the flashes gave me a clear count of each collision.

pixel_tracker_module.flavour: A qubit-array sensor that records the exact path of every charged particle crossing it. Each pixel is a qubit that flips when a particle passes, and the trail of flipped pixels traces a track. It is flat, cold and delicate.
pixel_tracker_module.discovery: I needed to see particle tracks, not just flashes. In the Femto Fabricator I laid Qubits and Quantum Dots on a Cherenkov Wafer with Superconducting Solder. Every passing particle flipped a line of pixels.

plasma_nozzle_tip.flavour: A converging magnetic nozzle that accelerates plasma to a few percent of the speed of light. Topological insulators guide the current around its throat and tachyon crystals keep the field ahead of the flow. It glows bright at the tip even when cold.
plasma_nozzle_tip.discovery: In the Femto Fabricator, I shaped a magnetic throat from Neutronium Plate, Topological Insulator and Metamaterial Sheet, and added a Tachyon Crystal to drive the field ahead of the plasma.

gravitic_lens_element.flavour: A dark-matter lens trimmed so its Einstein ring falls exactly where it is needed. Gravitational lensing bends light from distant objects into rings and arcs; this one is tuned to focus gravity on a chosen point. It looks like a faint distortion in empty air.
gravitic_lens_element.discovery: In the Metamaterial Weaver I trimmed a Dark Matter Lens with Metamaterial Sheet and Entangled Photon Pairs to measure the focus. Adjusting the Dark Matter, the Einstein ring settled exactly where I wanted it.

hawking_absorber_plate.flavour: Metamaterial tuned to soak up the thermal glow of an evaporating black hole. Hawking radiation has a characteristic spectrum, and this plate absorbs it perfectly. It is warm on its front face, cool on the back, and very black.
hawking_absorber_plate.discovery: Hawking radiation was leaking away from my experiments. In the Casimir Vacuum Press I bonded a Metamaterial Sheet to Neutronium Plate, tuning the metamaterial to the black hole spectrum.

error_correction_lattice.flavour: Thousands of physical qubits standing guard over one logical qubit. Each error is caught by the neighbours, which vote it out before it can spread. It is a delicate lattice of light, cold to touch, and remarkably stable.
error_correction_lattice.discovery: My qubits kept losing coherence. In the Neural Synthesizer, I let a Quantum Processor arrange Qubits around a Superposition Crystal, using Synaptic Fluid to learn which errors to vote out.

anchor_core.flavour: Negative mass pinned inside spacetime alloy. It holds the metric still while everything around it bends, a fixed point in curved space. It is heavy and light at once, and sits perfectly still no matter how hard I push it.
anchor_core.discovery: In the Graviton Condenser I set a Negative Mass Ingot inside Spacetime Alloy with Exotic Matter. The positive and negative curvatures cancelled, and the space inside stopped moving.

stabiliser_matrix.flavour: Compactified dimensions woven tight with quantum strings, so they stay rolled up under load. Without it, extra dimensions tend to unroll, and the laws of physics shift. It looks like a tight knot of light, faintly warm.
stabiliser_matrix.discovery: On the String Resonance Loom I wove Quantum Strings through a Calabi-Yau Manifold with a Topological Insulator and Exotic Matter. The compact dimensions held their shape even under pressure.

causal_shield_lattice.flavour: Chronosteel threaded with stored chronons. Paradoxes that strike it are deflected into somebody else's timeline instead of mine. It is cool, faintly ticking, and slightly out of sync with the world around it.
causal_shield_lattice.discovery: In the Chronon Field Inverter, I threaded Chronon Capacitors through Chronosteel with Chronon Gas. When a paradox hit the lattice, it slid off into another history and left mine alone.
